title: [Model fails to open] whisper_init_from_file_with_params_no_state
body:
Hello, everyone,

I decided to incorporate Whisper.cpp as a backend into my SoftWhisper frontend and it proved to be a wonderful decision.
However, some people are reporting whisper-cli fails to open their models even when the files are there. For example:

whisper_init_from_file_with_params_no_state: loading model from 'models/ggml-base.en.bin'
whisper_init_from_file_with_params_no_state: failed to open 'models/ggml-base.en.bin'
error: failed to initialize whisper context

One of the users stated that they are facing this issue even when calling whisper-cli directly (https://github.com/reporter/SoftWhisper/issues/4#issuecomment-2743389650), so I suppose the issue is related to the whisper-cli directly, not my graphical interface.

Could you help me understand what could be causing this? I haven't changed the whisper.cpp source. The only thing I did was to build it with Vulkan support.

Unfortunately, I've been unable to reproduce this because whisper-cli works just fine for me, even if I change folders around.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi, @participant1,

That fixed the bug in my computer, but it turned out there was another issue: the cmake is trying to always build with the native featureset, and my processor uses AVX 512.  

I tried to disable it, but the cmake file at ggml\src\ggml-cpu\cmake\FindSIMD.cmake will try to force AVX512. 

After debugging with a few friends, one of them suggested me to comment out a few lines at this file, which finally allowed me to toggle AVX512 to disable it, which fixes the issue.

Here is the patch: https://pastebin.com/kRWUEPSs

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> That fixed the bug in my computer, but it turned out there was another issue: the cmake is trying to always build with the native featureset, and my processor uses AVX 512.

Could you show us the CMake command and options you are using to build?  

It sounds like you might be compiling with `GGML_NATIVE=ON` (the default) which will query the host CPU for features it has available and enable those features. The produced binary might not be portable depending on the target CPU's that it is intended for. 

It should be possible to set `-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF` to disable this and then one has to set the features to enable explicitly (if any). But when I tried this to make sure, I noticed that setting that alone is not sufficient. I also needed to set the environment variable `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`:
```console
env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1234567890 cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
cmake --build build
```
This was a little surprising to me that setting `GGML_NATIVE=OFF` alone was not enough and I've opened https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/issues/2930 to try to understand this better.

Hi, @participant1, 

I'm not using -DGGML_NATIVE. Here are the flags I used:

cmake -B build -DGGML_VULKAN=1 -DGGML_AVX512=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VBMI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VNNI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_BF16=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE=ON

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
So when you build with the command you specified:
```console
cmake -B build -DGGML_VULKAN=1 -DGGML_AVX512=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VBMI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VNNI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_BF16=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE=ON
```
This will actually cause `GGML_NATIVE` to be `ON`, as this is the default setting, and you should see something like the following in the CMake output:
```console
-- x86 detected
-- Adding CPU backend variant ggml-cpu: -march=native 
```
If you instead try setting the environment variable `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` this will disable `GGML_NATIVE`:
```console
env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1234567890 cmake -S . -B build                               
cmake --build build
...
-- x86 detected
-- Adding CPU backend variant ggml-cpu: -msse4.2 GGML_SSE42
```
If you now want to enable a specific feature you have to do so explicitly:
```console
env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1234567890 cmake -S . -B build -DGGML_AVX=ON
...
-- x86 detected
-- Adding CPU backend variant ggml-cpu: -msse4.2;-mavx GGML_SSE42;GGML_AVX
```
Can you give this a try (removing the edits to CMakeLists.txt mentioned above) and see if this produces a build that works for your situation?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Either way, here are the results:

Thanks for providing this. 

Looking at the output this looks like what I would have expected:
```console
-- x86 detected
-- Adding CPU backend variant ggml-cpu: /arch:AVX2 GGML_AVX2;GGML_FMA;GGML_F16C;__BMI2__;GGML_BMI2
```
The instruction sets included are the ones included for [AVX2](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/blob/30cf30ca8248b659ae7eb9b0f73f83899e21689f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt#L209-L211) for MSVC. 

And notice that this time there is no output like the following lines:
```console
-- x86 detected
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX_1
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX_1 - Success
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX2_1
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX2_1 - Success
-- Performing Test HAS_FMA_1
-- Performing Test HAS_FMA_1 - Success
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX512_1
-- Performing Test HAS_AVX512_1 - Success
```
The `Performing Test ...` statements are coming from [CheckSourceRuns](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/blob/30cf30ca8248b659ae7eb9b0f73f83899e21689f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/cmake/FindSIMD.cmake#L1), which is called by [FindSIMD.cmake](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/blob/30cf30ca8248b659ae7eb9b0f73f83899e21689f/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt#L172):
```console
        if (MSVC)
            # instruction set detection for MSVC only
            if (GGML_NATIVE)
                include(ggml-cpu/cmake/FindSIMD.cmake)
            endif ()
```
So what I think was happening in your case is that `GGML_NATIVE` was enabled (which is the default value), and this was causing the issue of including instructions for `AVX512` as they were detected to be supported by your CPU. Using something like the above options should enable you to build without including AVX512.

Maybe setting GGML_NATIVE to off if custom flags were set would be a good choice?
